newsitem.title: JAPAN: Chinon to get support from Kodak, Hachijuni Bank.
newsitem.headline: Chinon to get support from Kodak, Hachijuni Bank.

text.p: Chinon Industries Inc said on Thursday that the Eastman Kodak group and Hachijuni Bank Ltd had agreed to support Chinon's restructuring efforts.
Under the restructuring program, Chinon will allocate 9.91 million new shares worth 1.88 billion yen to Eastman Kodak and its group companies, with payment due on September 1.
Kodak is already the top shareholder of Chinon, a maker of information equipment, with a 12.18 percent stake.
The new allocation will raise that to 50.1 percent, Chinon said.
Hachijuni Bank is Chinon's main bank and has a 4.2 percent stake in the company.
Hachijuni Bank has basically agreed to accept a request from Chinon to forgive debts of 4.25 billion yen, a Chinon statement said, although it gave no further details.
Chinon also said it plans to sell assets, such as land and buildings, for a profit of 1.86 billion yen.
The company has posted parent current losses and net losses since 1991/92, as it failed to move quickly to lower prices on floppy disc drives and CD-ROM drives, a Chinon spokesman said.
The company has not revised its November forecast of a parent current profit of 1.50 billion yen and a net loss of 4.95 billion yen for 1996/97. It is expected to announce its results in May.

But Chinon said it expects the restructuring plan to let it post parent current profit of 415 million yen and net profit of 6.65 billion yen in 1997/98, and current profit of 950 million yen and net profit of 900 million yen in 1998/99, the spokesman said.
Chinon also said it would form a new company, tentatively named Chinon Tech, on May 8.
Chinon will transfer most of its divisions, including optics, medical equipment and computer software, to the new company. Chinon will concentrate on its digital camera business.

The new company, capitalised at 10 million yen, will be owned 80 percent by Yukichi Ishigaki, the president of Chinon, and 10 percent by Chinon. The statement said no owner had been decided yet for the other 10 percent.
As a result, Chinon Tech will take over 400 of Chinon's 550 employees.
